explanation: Purge and clear-first both call ClearKey (lines 179, 182), which marks the key cleared and destroys its values; the only difference is that clear-first first forgets the old clearance so it sorts before values, then re-adds the key's direct non-deletion values. The rule says only clear-first 'marks the key cleared', implying purge does not. Also the third choice is reached only when a value name is typed: EditPolDelete refuses a blank name with 'You must enter a value name.' (EditPolDelete.vb 12-15), and confirms nothing until a choice is selected (line 11). State the outcome of each choice and the name requirement.

The language folder is named from Globalization.CultureInfo.CurrentCulture.Name (line 104), the regional-format culture, not the display language. Say which, in business words. Also, when the language is not en-US the en-US folder is moved unconditionally (line 110): if the package lacks it the move fails at 'move the ADMX files', unlike the optional own-language folder (line 107). The rule should state that asymmetry.

Omits what happens after a confirmed key Forget: the list is rebuilt and selection returns to the forgotten key's parent (all ancestors reselected in turn, lines 214, 230-234), or nothing is selected for a top-level key and button states are refreshed (line 236). Forgetting a value has its own rule with the return-to-key outcome; this one should state the key case.

The validity and availability checks (this and businessrule-22829021656307913118) are restated wholesale inside the add-key rule businessrule-82031918738264447842, which states the same refusals with their messages. One decision is split into three rules; keep the checks inside the add-key rule (they are called only from there) or make the add-key rule refer to them without repeating the conditions.

Duplicates the cancel clauses already in the add-value rule and the edit-value rule, and decidedAt spans a whole prompt function that also holds the unsupported-kind refusal and the data conversion. A cancel with nothing returned is the shared contract of PromptForNewValueData; either fold into those rules or scope this one to the prompt function alone.

says: EditPolDelete refuses to confirm the single-value delete when no value name is typed ('You must enter a value name.'), and confirms nothing until one of the three choices is selected. This gates the key-delete outcome of ButtonDeleteValue_Click and is written nowhere; add it to the delete-key rule or its own rule, citing the dialog's OK handler.

The download leaves partial results on failure: there is no rollback, so files already moved into the destination stay, and the scratch folder under local app data is deleted only on the last step (line 114), so any earlier failure leaves it behind. A failure at 'remove temporary files' happens after the files were already installed. A reader deciding whether a failed download is safe to retry needs this; the failure rule says only that the person is told which step failed. Also no destination validation exists (empty or invalid text is passed on, failing at 'move the ADMX files'), and non-administrators skip ownership handling entirely and proceed.
